q: Put the cardinal movements of a vertex delivery in order, from the head entering the pelvis to delivery of the body.
key: Each movement fits the smallest diameter of the head to the widest diameter of the pelvic level it is passing: the inlet is widest from side to side and the outlet from front to back, so the head enters sideways, turns at the spines, extends under the symphysis, then untwists so the shoulders can follow.
items: Engagement: the widest diameter of the head passes through the pelvic inlet
It comes first because the head must enter the pelvis before anything else; it usually enters facing sideways, because the inlet is widest from side to side.
Descent: contractions and pushing drive the head down the birth canal
Descent continues through the rest of labor, but it must begin before the head meets the pelvic resistance that produces the movements that follow.
Flexion: the chin tucks onto the chest as the head meets the pelvic floor
Resistance from the cervix and pelvic floor flexes the descending head, so its smallest diameter leads before it reaches the spines and turns.
Internal rotation: the occiput turns toward the pubic symphysis at the ischial spines
The midpelvis and outlet are widest from front to back, so the flexed head turns there, which it must do before it can pass under the symphysis.
Extension: the occiput pivots under the symphysis and the face sweeps over the perineum
Only an occiput that has rotated to the front can pivot under the symphysis, so extension follows internal rotation and delivers the head.
External rotation: the born head turns back to face sideways (restitution)
Once the head is free, it untwists to line up with the shoulders, which are now turning into the front-to-back diameter of the outlet.
Expulsion: the anterior shoulder slips under the symphysis, then the posterior shoulder and body follow
The shoulders can deliver only after they rotate into the long axis of the outlet, so expulsion is last; impaction of the anterior shoulder here is shoulder dystocia.
